title: Seasonal FORECAST.ETS centers 2p sliding moving-average initials, starts smoothing at j=0, and linearly interpolates fractional CONFINT variance
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527, seasonal AAA FORECAST.ETS builds initial state over m = min(len, 5 * p) observations (extending histories shorter than ceil(3.5 * p) by tau = sum_q regression_slope(phase_q) / (p * p) via raw-moment slopes). It computes a subtract-first 2*p sliding moving average sum = (sum - e[t - 1]) + e[t + 2*p - 1], T[t] = sum / (2*p), averages detrended e[t + p/2 - 1] - T[t] per phase to form raw[q], centers seasons[q] = raw[q] - center with pre-centered initial level = (y[0] - raw[0]) + center, and sets initial trend T_0 = regression_slope(e[j] - seasons[j % p]). The smoothing loop starts at t = -1 (level = initial.level - initial.trend) and runs from j = 0, so err[0] enters MAE, RMSE, SSE, and state updates. FORECAST.ETS.STAT types 1-3 show Excel stores 6-digit rounded binary64 smoothing constants (such as 0.001, 0.0833333, 0.166667); seasonal_general re-centers seasons and adds them via x87 PC64; and FORECAST.ETS.CONFINT linearly interpolates mse * horizon_variance at fractional horizons (from 0 on h in (0, 1)) before sqrt and x87 multiplication by z.
basis: Measured across nx3's live Excel 16.0.20527 frozen holdouts (frozen_ets_pred.json 32 of 48 vs 1 of 48; frozen_confint_frac_pred.json 33 of 40 vs 16 of 40) and cb4's FORECAST.ETS.STAT measurements. On the full witness banks, FORECAST.ETS moved from 2,640 to 2,959 of 2,959 (+319, worst ULP 1,440 -> 0), FORECAST.ETS.CONFINT from 4,001 to 4,355 of 4,355 (+354, worst ULP 736 -> 0), FORECAST.ETS.STAT stayed 2,955 of 2,955, and FORECAST.ETS.SEASONALITY stayed 2,958 of 2,958.
inferred: That Excel executes this exact sliding moving average, j=0 indexing, and fractional variance interpolation is inferred from matching all 12,227 bank rows and the unseen frozen holdouts.
